task_instance: Define a minimal Neon Function (a Hono app with a GET / and GET /todos handler) in neon.ts + src/index.ts, install the Neon Functions tooling (neonctl, hono, @neon/config, @neon/functions, @neon/env, drizzle-orm, pg), and run it with the local `neon dev` loop, verifying the HTTP handler responds as expected (the skill's stated deliverable: 'a working local neon dev loop').
blocker_detail: Full production deployment (neon deploy / neon functions deploy, obtaining a public invocation_url on aws-us-east-2 etc., and DATABASE_URL injection) requires an authenticated Neon account/project (neon auth, neon link, neon checkout), which is account-bound and out of scope per the safety rules. The local dev loop, which the skill explicitly lists as an acceptable deliverable, does not require an account and was fully exercised.
evidence: Installed packages via `npm install neonctl hono drizzle-orm pg @neon/config @neon/functions @neon/env` (166 packages). Created /tmp/.../neon.ts declaring a `todos` function pointing at src/index.ts, and src/index.ts exporting a Hono app with `GET /` and `GET /todos`. Ran `npx neon dev --source src/index.ts --port 4322` in the background; it printed 'Neon Functions dev server' and served on http://localhost:4322, warning only that no Neon branch is linked (so DATABASE_URL is not injected, as expected without an account). Verified the deliverable by curling the running server: `curl http://localhost:4322/` returned 'Neon + Hono local test', and `curl http://localhost:4322/todos` returned '[{"id":1,"text":"sample"}]'. This confirms the `neon dev` local development loop described in the skill works end-to-end for a function definition.
